correctness.rationale: The actual system is xdot=a*y, ydot=x+z^2, zdot=b+c*x+d*z with a,d<0, c!=0. Direct independent SymPy differentiation confirms Q=z-c*y satisfies Qdot=Delta/(4c)-c(z-d/(2c))^2. For Delta<0 it drifts at nonzero uniform speed, impossible on any bounded forward-complete orbit; for Delta>=0 equilibrium roots z=(d±sqrtDelta)/(2c) produce compact singletons. At Delta=0, monotonic bounded Q on a bounded forward orbit and the invariant zero-derivative locus z=z* force x=-z*^2, y=0, yielding global-on-bounded-orbits convergence and unique compact two-sided invariant set. Invariant measures satisfy E[(z-z*)^2]=Delta/(4c^2). Linearization at equality has lambda(lambda^2-d lambda-a) with two strictly stable roots. Quadratic center graph v=-(d/c)u-u^2+O(u^3), w=(d/a)u^2+O(u^3) yields udot=-c u^2+O(u^3); one-sided convergent center trajectories obey t*u ->1/c, and standard stable-foliation tracking transfers this to all bounded convergent orbits except the strong-stable set. Boundary case c<0 and strong-stable exponential decay handled. No claim about solutions escaping to infinity.

The unique critical stationary law and universal trajectory-level 1/t relaxation outside a codimension-one center direction describe the phase boundary and are meaningful in bifurcation theory. Both sharpness and scope are natural; no general chaos existence is claimed.
